title: Sports roundup: FKF hits back at McCarthy, Brentford thrash Everton, US and UK to host Women's World Cups
key_points: FKF says it never picks the Harambee Stars squad and that McCarthy's November pay was made early.
Brentford beat Everton 4-0 on Monday night to close the Premier League round.
FIFA gave the 2031 Women's World Cup to the US, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, and 2035 to the UK, Anadolu reported.
Big game on Sunday: Arsenal v Manchester City.
content:
Here is the latest sports news, starting at home.

Harambee Stars: FKF and McCarthy row grows

The Football Kenya Federation (FKF) has rejected claims that its officials interfere in choosing the Harambee Stars squad, Dawan Africa reported. FKF Head of Communications Jeff Kinyanjui said on X that only the coach and his technical staff pick the players.

The row started after Kenya lost 2-1 to South Africa at Nyayo Stadium on November 17 in an AFCON qualifier. Coach Benni McCarthy then complained about hotels, meals, transport and late payments to players, The Star reported. He said the players came close to a strike before they were paid.

Kinyanjui said on local radio that McCarthy was trying to shift attention from his comments after the match. He said McCarthy's November salary was paid in advance, and that the government, not FKF, pays the coach. Dawan Africa noted that in March 2025, FKF President Hussein Mohamed said the federation would pay McCarthy, according to K24 Digital.

McCarthy apologised on November 19 for his reaction to online criticism after the loss. Kenya is third in its group with two points from four games. The team is already in AFCON 2027 as a co-host with Uganda and Tanzania, and FIFA ranks Kenya 115th in the world, Kenya Today reported.

Premier League: Brentford 4-0 Everton

Brentford beat Everton 4-0 at home on Monday night to finish the weekend's games.

The weekend's other results were:

  • Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United
  • Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal
  • Chelsea 1-4 Leeds
  • Manchester City 1-1 Fulham
  • Tottenham 2-0 Ipswich
  • Coventry 3-2 Crystal Palace
  • Bournemouth 2-0 Nottingham Forest
  • Aston Villa 0-0 Sunderland
  • Hull 2-0 Brighton

Coming up: Nottingham Forest v Chelsea on Friday, November 27, and Arsenal v Manchester City on Sunday, November 29.

Women's World Cup hosts chosen

FIFA has given the 2031 Women's World Cup to the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica. It gave the 2035 tournament to the United Kingdom, Anadolu Agency reported. Both bids had no rivals, and the vote was held at an online FIFA meeting.

The 2031 tournament will be the first with 48 teams, up from 32, and will have 104 matches. ESPN reported that Jamaica's matches will be the first senior World Cup games played in the Caribbean.

Why it matters: more teams means more places for African women's teams, including Kenya's Harambee Starlets.

Also in sport

  • Spain's LaLiga said a cyberattack between November 14 and 16 exposed personal details of fans registered on its digital services. It says the attack has been stopped.
